audit.whatIsWrong: FABRICATED ABILITY NAME. 'Repeating Dashes' is not an Ambessa ability. It was the matchup's focus ability and appeared in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, ahead, loading, focus.text, three phase whys, five breakdown fields, dosFull[0], and five report entries. Ambessa's real kit is Drakehound's Step (P), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q), Repudiation (W), Lacerate (E), Public Execution (R).
audit.why: packet.defects explicitly flags that the entry never names any of Ambessa's abilities. The dash is Drakehound's Step, a passive that triggers off issuing a move or attack command during a cast — it has no cooldown of its own, so 'track its cooldown' was advice a player could not act on. The trackable cooldown is Public Execution at 130/115/100.
audit.corrected: Real names written throughout, and the tracked cooldown moved to Public Execution. Its decisive property is now stated: it blinks to the FARTHEST enemy champion in a line and suppresses on arrival, so standing behind the wave is not a screen. Lacerate's 13s and Titan's Wrath's flat 12s carry the trade timings.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicted the whys sitting beside it on four of seven rows. whys[1] says 'I win the short trade' under an 'Ambessa' token; whys[2] calls level 3 'my cleanest kill window of the lane' under 'Ambessa'; whys[3] says Nautilus zones her off the wave under 'Skill'; whys[4] says 'concede 6' under 'Skill'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart gives Nautilus rows 1-3 and Ambessa row 4, matching those whys exactly. I did NOT take the packet chart's rows 5-6 (Skill/Nautilus): whys[5], the late block and the 41.18% win rate all say Ambessa owns the item phases, and packet.defects itself flags the packet chart as too Nautilus-favourable overall.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa in BOTH layers as matched pairs, ratings realigned (6/10, 7/10 at the level-3 kill window, 6/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike was described without a number, and the level-6 spike attributed her win to 'her dash chain and W burst' spacing-cancelling Depth Charge.
audit.why: The reason level 6 flips is Public Execution itself — a 130s blink to the farthest champion in a line that suppresses on arrival. That is a far more specific and more actionable fact than 'her mobility'. Repudiation's own rule (increased damage if it blocked non-minion damage while bracing) is what actually punishes a player who trades into it.
audit.corrected: Level-6 spike and phases[4].why rebuilt on Public Execution's blink-to-farthest and suppression at 130s; wants.foe[1] rebuilt on Repudiation's block-then-slam rule; breakdown.mid keyed to Lacerate's 13s.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t and breakdown.late told the player anti-heal is core because 'his healing fights your grind'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Public Execution describes a blink, suppression, a slam, damage and a stun — no healing. The 'heal' derived flag on her R contradicts the description, and per the standing rule the description wins. The missingInteractions 'needs-antiheal' entry rests on that same misfiring flag. Buying Grievous Wounds into Ambessa on this evidence would be a wasted item slot.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal replaced with early armour — her whole combo is physical — in both fields.
sources: enemyKit R text vs enemyKit R heal flag

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0].d gave no tell for when her combo starts.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step is an auto-attack empower triggered by inputting a move or attack command during a cast — the dash wind-up, not an ability icon, is the visible cue.
audit.corrected: Don't now names the Drakehound's Step dash as the step-back cue.

edits.before: I keep the edge at 4-5 while my W shield and E scale, but level 6 is where this lane turns. Depth Charge looks like a guaranteed pick, except her mobility lets her cancel my spacing mid-combo and her W bursts me down through the knock-up if I commit without my full chain. Don't throw R as an opener hoping to solo her — she'll weave out of the follow-up and win the trade. Use 6 to set up my jungler, not to 1v1 her.

notes: 'Repeating Dashes' was a fabricated ability name used as this matchup's tracked cooldown in roughly twenty fields across both layers; all of them are corrected here. Two derived flags on Ambessa contradict Riot's own text and were NOT used: Repudiation (W) carries a 'grounding' flag the description does not support (shield, brace, slam only), and Public Execution (R) carries a 'heal' flag the description does not support — which means the missingInteractions 'needs-antiheal' entry for this matchup rests on a bad flag, and I removed the two anti-heal build instructions rather than reinforce them. NOT asserted because the kit files do not cover it: whether Public Execution's suppression can be cleansed or QSS'd, and whether tenacity shortens it. Sample is 17 games at 41.18%.
